title: The Audubon, a cracked voice, and the Palace
summary: His voice cracked at the Audubon so he took up dancing; three months later they were the first Negro act held over at the Palace on a big bill.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: About two weeks later I played the Aubodon Theater, 168th Street and Broadway. Now, there my voice cracked at the Abodon Theater and I thought I should take up dancing, I hadn't danced a leg yet, to compensate for my voice I'd do a dance, that's what I thought.

About three months after we played the Columbia Theater we played the Palace and no negro played that Palace, man, for months and months, they told me we wouldn't get in there. We played it. In less time -- they were still getting in the Palace when we played it. However, we played the Palace. First Negro act held over a second week in the Palace Theater. We went on the stage with such people like Ray Samuels, Clayton Jackson and (Jimmy) Durante, (Fred) Warings Pennsylvanians,

Tom Patricola, the dancer, Jack Donahue. Look, we had a big bill, eight acts and after the first week we had to be placed on No. 2, next to closing, about the third act. They had to put us on next to closing because nobody wanted to follow us. We turned out to be the next to closing act from that point on.
Then we got on the Orpheum circuit.
